title: TMB modeling with R and C++
summary: Custom likelihoods, automatic differentiation, latent-variable integration and forecasting, with original R/C++ models and a separately prepared Python bridge.

lessons.title: Why a C++ objective is called from R
lessons.outcome: Trace an observation through the objective, optimizer and returned estimate.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which evaluates a sum-of-squares objective and its gradient at two means for two small datasets. Compiling a C++ objective and calling it from R happens only in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project: `R/compile.R` builds its nine model templates and `R/api.R` calls them through `TMB::MakeADFun`.
lessons.verification: The gradient n*mu - sum(y) is zero at the sample mean 3 of (1, 2, 6), and replacing 6 with 9 moves the minimizer to 4.

lessons.title: Template types and the objective contract
lessons.outcome: Separate data shapes from optimized parameters and detect a malformed design.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a design-matrix and coefficient shape contract with base-R matrices. Typed `DATA_` and `PARAMETER_` declarations are compiled only in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, for example `DATA_MATRIX(X)` and `PARAMETER_VECTOR(beta)` in `models/regression.cpp`.
lessons.verification: The design has one row per observation and one column per coefficient, and a one-column design is rejected for the two-coefficient vector.

lessons.title: The full Gaussian negative log likelihood
lessons.outcome: Derive and check the normalized Gaussian objective and its scale estimate.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which evaluates the full Gaussian negative log likelihood and checks it against `dnorm` and against duplicated data. The compiled version is `models/normal_mean.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, and its `tests/acceptance.R` compares `obj$fn` with the same base-R sum of `dnorm` terms.
lessons.verification: The normalized negative log likelihood equals minus the sum of `dnorm` log densities, and tripling the data triples it without moving the mean.

lessons.title: Stable parameter constraints
lessons.outcome: Use unconstrained coordinates without changing the inferential target.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which optimizes a log standard deviation and tabulates the tanh correlation transform. The compiled templates in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project use the same unconstrained coordinates, for example `log_sigma` and `phi_raw` in `models/ar1.cpp`.
lessons.verification: `optimize` over log sigma returns a positive standard deviation, and the tanh derivative at 8 is below 1e-5, showing how flat the transform becomes.

lessons.title: Compile, load and isolate an owned library
lessons.outcome: Explain exactly which source and native library a model evaluation uses.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which fingerprints two source-description files with `tools::md5sum`; it compiles nothing. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `R/compile.R` runs `TMB::compile`, and `make_objective()` in `R/api.R` loads the library with `dyn.load` and refuses a different library already loaded under the same name.
lessons.verification: Two source descriptions that differ by one character get different MD5 fingerprints; no library is compiled or loaded.

lessons.title: MakeADFun values and gradients
lessons.outcome: Check an analytic gradient against central differences, the same oracles the prepared project uses to test TMB's automatic derivatives.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks the analytic Gaussian gradient against central differences at two points, so it does not call `MakeADFun`. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `make_objective()` in `R/api.R` calls `TMB::MakeADFun`, and `tests/acceptance.R` compares `obj$fn` with the base-R likelihood and `obj$gr` with a central-difference gradient.
lessons.verification: Central differences with step 1e-4 match the analytic Gaussian gradient to within 1e-5 at both test points.

lessons.title: nlminb and optimization evidence
lessons.outcome: Assess a fit using objective, gradient, status and multiple starting points.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which runs `nlminb` itself, on a base-R Gaussian objective from two starting points. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `fit_objective()` in `R/api.R` passes TMB's `obj$fn` and `obj$gr` to the same optimizer and records the maximum absolute gradient.
lessons.verification: `nlminb` from the starts (-2, 0) and (8, 2) reaches the same estimate to within 1e-4, and each run prints its final gradient.

lessons.title: Hessian, curvature and weak identification
lessons.outcome: Explain when inverse curvature can and cannot support standard errors.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares eigenvalues of ordinary and nearly collinear cross-product matrices and applies the delta method. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/acceptance.R` calls `TMB::sdreport` and requires a positive-definite Hessian (`pdHess`), and `fit_objective()` uses `stats::optimHess` for its optional Newton correction.
lessons.verification: The nearly collinear cross-product has a condition number above 1e8, while the transformed interval for exp(s) stays positive.

lessons.title: REPORT versus ADREPORT
lessons.outcome: Choose plain diagnostics or derivative-aware uncertainty for each output.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which computes delta-method variances for transformed parameters. The templates in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project declare both kinds of output, for example `REPORT(residual)` and `ADREPORT(sigma)` in `models/normal_mean.cpp`; `tests/acceptance.R` reads `obj$report()` and calls `TMB::sdreport`.
lessons.verification: The numerical Jacobian of exp at log 2 matches exp(s) to 1e-8, and the covariance used for the ratio's standard error is positive definite.

lessons.title: A nonlinear trend likelihood
lessons.outcome: Fit and interpret a nonlinear mean without confusing interpolation and extrapolation.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which fits the decay curve with `nlminb` on a base-R likelihood. The compiled version is `models/nonlinear.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, which `tests/acceptance.R` fits with `fit_objective()` and checks against the generating amplitude, rate and offset.
lessons.verification: `nlminb` converges on the decay curve and recovers the generating rate 0.6 to within 0.03.

lessons.title: Count and censored likelihood terms
lessons.outcome: Write normalized terms that reflect what was actually observed.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which evaluates Poisson-exposure and censored, delayed-entry Weibull contributions. The compiled versions are `models/poisson_exposure.cpp` and `models/censored_weibull.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project; `tests/acceptance.R` checks their values against `dpois` and the closed form 2.5 + log 2.
lessons.verification: The censored, delayed-entry Weibull (shape 1) negative log likelihood equals 2.5 + log 2 exactly, unlike the version that treats every time as an event.

lessons.title: Fixed effects and latent random effects
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a latent joint objective from its marginal likelihood.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which evaluates the marginal Gaussian likelihood through a Cholesky factor and tabulates shrinkage. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `models/random_intercept.cpp` is built with `random = "u"`, and `tests/acceptance.R` checks TMB's Laplace objective against the exact Gaussian marginal likelihood.
lessons.verification: The marginal covariance is positive definite, and the shrinkage factor is larger for a group of 20 than for a group of 2.

lessons.title: Deriving the Laplace approximation
lessons.outcome: Derive the integrated objective and test its exact Gaussian special case.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares the Laplace value with numerical quadrature for Gaussian and quartic integrands. TMB's own Laplace approximation runs only in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, where `tests/acceptance.R` compares the random-intercept objective with its exact Gaussian integral.
lessons.verification: The Laplace value is exact for the Gaussian integrand at tau 0.5 and 2, while quadrature shows its error once a quartic term is added.

lessons.title: Inner and outer convergence
lessons.outcome: Diagnose latent-mode failure separately from fixed-parameter convergence.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which takes a Newton step on a quadratic and compares limited and full `nlminb` runs. TMB's inner optimization of latent effects runs only in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, for the models built with `random = "u"` (`random_intercept`, `ar1` and `panel_trend`).
lessons.verification: One Newton step from (10, -7) solves the quadratic exactly, while a one-iteration `nlminb` run leaves a visible gradient on the double-well objective.

lessons.title: AR(1) states and sparse precision
lessons.outcome: Connect a time-series recurrence to covariance, precision and TMB density.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which builds the tridiagonal AR(1) precision matrix and checks that it inverts the covariance. The compiled latent AR(1) model is `models/ar1.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, and `tests/acceptance.R` compares its Laplace objective with the exact stationary-covariance likelihood.
lessons.verification: The tridiagonal AR(1) precision matrix inverts the stationary covariance to within 1e-12 for phi = -0.6 and 0.6.

lessons.title: Independent panels and parameter ownership
lessons.outcome: Choose between separate panel fits and one shared likelihood.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which contrasts pooled and panel averages and block versus shared covariance matrices. The compiled panel model is `models/panel_trend.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, which `tests/acceptance.R` fits with four groups and their latent offsets.
lessons.verification: The pooled mean equals the size-weighted average of panel means, and a shared intercept adds covariance 0.2 between otherwise independent blocks.

lessons.title: Shared effects versus separable blocks
lessons.outcome: Prove when group-level Laplace contributions can be added and when they cannot.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks log-determinant additivity for block-diagonal covariance and shows where it fails. The separately prepared `tmb-local` project has no separate template for this comparison; `models/panel_trend.cpp` shows the shared case, with common trend parameters and one latent offset per group.
lessons.verification: The block-diagonal log determinant equals the sum of the block log determinants, and coupled variables break that additivity.

lessons.title: Prediction and uncertainty with sdreport
lessons.outcome: Report distinct intervals for a mean, a latent state and a future observation.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which tabulates AR(1) forecast means and variances and a simplified new-group uncertainty, so it does not call `sdreport`. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/acceptance.R` fits `models/panel_trend.cpp`, whose template ADREPORTs `prediction`, `sigma` and `tau`, and calls `TMB::sdreport(..., getReportCovariance = FALSE)`, requiring a positive-definite Hessian.
lessons.verification: Forecast innovation variance grows with horizon, and the new-group observation SD exceeds the intercept standard error.

lessons.title: Simulate, recover and criticize
lessons.outcome: Use reproducible simulations to evaluate an estimator and its uncertainty claims.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which runs a 200-replicate coverage simulation with `rnorm`. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` calls `obj$simulate()` on the compiled normal model, whose template has a `SIMULATE` block, and runs `TMB::checkConsistency()`.
lessons.verification: Independent replicates print coverage near 0.95 with Monte Carlo SE about 0.015, while a shared random shift pushes the nominal interval's coverage below 0.8.

lessons.title: Parallel accumulators and OpenMP
lessons.outcome: Partition an independent likelihood sum so that a parallel evaluation preserves the objective and its derivatives.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks that a partitioned likelihood sum equals the serial sum and tabulates thread requests. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `models/parallel_gaussian.cpp` is compiled with OpenMP, and `tests/acceptance.R` compares its value and gradient under `TMB::openmp(1, ...)` and `TMB::openmp(2, ...)`.
lessons.verification: The likelihood summed over two chunks equals the serial sum, and averaging per-chunk means instead of dividing by n gives the wrong mean loss.

lessons.title: AFModel as a historical design case
lessons.outcome: Translate a historical modeling architecture into an original, inspectable panel example.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which tabulates a decaying trend with panel offsets and AR(1) residual forecasts. The separately prepared `tmb-local` project compiles the trend and autoregressive pieces as `models/panel_trend.cpp` and `models/ar1.cpp`; no AFModel code is compiled.
lessons.verification: Panel A's AR(1) residual forecasts shrink toward zero at every horizon (phi = 0.6) around a decaying trend with panel offsets.

lessons.title: Pandas, NumPy and R conversion
lessons.outcome: Define and test a typed data contract before crossing the Python/R boundary.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks row identity, missing values, factor levels and a UTC timestamp in an R data frame. pandas and rpy2 conversion runs only in the Python bridge of the separately prepared `tmb-local` project (`python/bridge.py`), checked by `tests/bridge_acceptance.py`.
lessons.verification: Row IDs are unique and values finite in the valid frame, a missing response is rejected, factor levels keep their declared order and the timestamp is UTC.

lessons.title: Python to a compiled TMB boundary
lessons.outcome: Design a narrow request to a prepared compiled model that keeps execution, data and native pointers isolated.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a request's parameter order and row identity. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `python/bridge.py` sends such requests to the compiled models through rpy2, and `tests/bridge_acceptance.py` checks the round trip.
lessons.verification: Parameters arrive in the declared order (mu, log_sigma), theta has length two and returned row IDs keep their original unsorted order.

lessons.title: A nonlinear forecast and uncertainty dossier
lessons.outcome: Assemble a reproducible fit, forecast and limitations report for a synthetic panel.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which tabulates trend forecasts with group offsets and known-group versus new-group noise. The compiled forecast model is `models/panel_trend.cpp` in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, whose ADREPORTed `prediction` is summarized by `TMB::sdreport` in `tests/acceptance.R`.
lessons.verification: Group offsets put sensor A's forecasts below and sensor B's above the new-group trend, and a new group's noise SD sqrt(sigma^2 + tau^2) exceeds a known group's.

lessons.title: From an empty template to a reviewed model
lessons.outcome: Separate generated scaffolding from a scientifically complete likelihood.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a declared data and parameter schema. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` prints the scaffold from `TMB::template()` and the interface that `TMB::Rinterface()` derives from `models/normal_mean.cpp`.
lessons.verification: The response length matches the design rows and beta has one entry per design column; a column list with the same shape but different meaning is flagged.

lessons.title: MakeADFun maps, profiles and safe data changes
lessons.outcome: Explain which construction options change parameter dimension, target or recorded operations.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which reconstructs a full parameter vector from a `map`-style factor, so it does not call `MakeADFun`. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` builds a `TMB::MakeADFun` object with `map = list(log_sigma = factor(NA))` and profiles `mu` with `TMB::tmbprofile`.
lessons.verification: A `map`-style factor rebuilds (3, 3, 7) from one free value, tying the first two parameters and fixing the third.

lessons.title: CppAD, TMBad and derivative order
lessons.outcome: Choose an AD framework for a specific tested derivative target.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks first and second finite-difference derivatives of a smooth function. The separately prepared `tmb-local` project compiles every model with `framework = "CppAD"` in `R/compile.R`; no TMBad build is part of the project.
lessons.verification: Central differences match the first derivative of exp(x) + x^4 to within 1e-6 at -0.4 and 0.7, and the printed derivatives of x^4 end at the constant 24.

lessons.title: Reporting objects and uncertainty controls
lessons.outcome: Read report objects without losing shape, estimand or uncertainty assumptions.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which computes a contrast standard error and compares a transformed mean with a mean of transforms. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` calls `TMB::sdreport(..., getReportCovariance = FALSE)` and prints its `summary`, `as.list` and `print` forms.
lessons.verification: The contrast standard error uses the full covariance, and the lognormal mean exp(m + v/2) exceeds the transformed mean exp(m).

lessons.title: Likelihood profiles versus slices
lessons.outcome: Explain nuisance reoptimization and derive a profile-likelihood interval.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares a profile with a slice for a correlated quadratic and contrasts transformed and delta-method intervals. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` profiles `mu` with `TMB::tmbprofile` and plots the profile to a temporary file.
lessons.verification: The profile (1 - rho^2)a^2/2 never exceeds the slice a^2/2, and the transformed log-scale interval differs from the symmetric delta interval by more than 0.1.

lessons.title: Profile interval roots and boundary cases
lessons.outcome: Find confidence endpoints by a stated likelihood-rise equation.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which finds profile-interval roots with `uniroot` and checks them against the exact interval. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` compares `confint()` of a `TMB::tmbprofile` result and `TMB::tmbroot()` with the exact interval 3.5 ± 1.96.
lessons.verification: `uniroot` finds both likelihood-rise endpoints to within 1e-4 of the exact interval, and an unconstrained interval for a positive parameter crosses zero.

lessons.title: Simulation APIs and score consistency
lessons.outcome: Distinguish generative consistency, estimation bias and approximation bias.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which simulates score statistics with `rnorm`. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` calls `obj$simulate()` and `TMB::checkConsistency(obj, n = 100)` on the compiled normal model.
lessons.verification: The mean and scale scores average near zero over 100 simulations, while the score that drops the normalizer averages below -10.

lessons.title: One-step-ahead predictive residuals
lessons.outcome: Construct diagnostics that respect observation ordering and conditioning.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which computes probability-integral-transform and randomized quantile residuals. No file in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project calls `oneStepPredict`, so this chapter's TMB usage is explanatory; the course API reference gives the pinned signature.
lessons.verification: Gaussian PIT residuals equal standardized forecast errors to 1e-12, and randomized quantile residuals for counts stay strictly inside (0, 1).

lessons.title: Normalizing a latent process
lessons.outcome: Explain why process normalization depends on parameters and affects estimation.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a Gaussian normalizing constant by quadrature and the null space of an intrinsic precision. No file in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project calls `TMB::normalize`, so this chapter's TMB usage is explanatory; the course API reference gives the pinned signature.
lessons.verification: The Gaussian kernel normalizes to 1 by quadrature for tau 0.5 and 2, and the intrinsic first-difference precision has the constant vector in its null space.

lessons.title: Alternative integration and sequential reduction
lessons.outcome: Compare integration strategies without confusing a documented helper with a supported public export.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares quadrature with the Laplace value and evaluates a discrete mixture marginal. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` only prints the `TMB::SR()` grid descriptor; no sequential-reduction fit runs there.
lessons.verification: Quadrature departs from the Laplace value once a quartic term is added, the two-component mixture marginal is positive and grid size grows as 20^d.

lessons.title: The inner Newton solver and its controls
lessons.outcome: Relate inner-optimizer controls to curvature and numerical failure modes.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which takes one Newton step on a quadratic and shifts an indefinite Hessian. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` solves a sparse quadratic with `TMB::newton` and reads a model's controls with `TMB::newtonOption(obj)`.
lessons.verification: One Newton step on the quadratic lands on the exact solution, and shifting the indefinite Hessian by 2I makes both eigenvalues positive.

lessons.title: Sparse symbolic analysis and factorization accuracy
lessons.outcome: Distinguish sparse structure, ordering and numerical solve accuracy.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which solves a tridiagonal system, checks a permuted solve and measures the error of dropping coupling. No file in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project calls `runSymbolicAnalysis`; sparse factorizations occur inside TMB's Laplace approximation for its latent models.
lessons.verification: A permuted tridiagonal solve restores the same solution to 1e-12, while dropping the off-diagonal coupling leaves a visible residual.

lessons.title: Compilation, ABI versions and native lifetime
lessons.outcome: Explain how native objects are built, loaded and retired with explicit version and process ownership.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which fingerprints two source-description files and prints the R version and platform; it compiles nothing. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `R/compile.R` compiles the models and writes a build record (`build-receipt.txt`) of R, TMB, Matrix, RcppEigen and architecture, and `tests/public_api.R` checks `TMB::dynlib()`, `TMB::config()` and `TMB::TMB.Version()` and releases objects with `TMB::FreeADFun()`.
lessons.verification: Two model revisions get different MD5 fingerprints and the printed build record names the R version and platform; nothing is compiled.

lessons.title: Debugging compiler and native failures
lessons.outcome: Separate R validation errors, compiler failures and native crashes during diagnosis.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which validates group indices before evaluation and models the build-failure decision. No file in the separately prepared `tmb-local` project calls `gdbsource`; its failure handling is input validation in `validate_inputs()` (`R/api.R`) and a stop on a nonzero `TMB::compile` status in `R/compile.R`.
lessons.verification: Valid zero-based group indices pass, an out-of-range index stops with an error and a failed build leads to the no-load state.

lessons.title: Benchmarking explicit and automatic parallelism
lessons.outcome: Plan a benchmark of a named operation that keeps thread policy and numerical correctness visible.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which tabulates illustrative timings and an Amdahl bound; its timings are hypothetical, not measurements. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/public_api.R` runs `TMB::benchmark(profile_obj, n = 10000, cores = 1)` with a fixed evaluation budget.
lessons.verification: With a serial fraction of 0.25 the Amdahl speedup can never exceed 4; the timing table is labeled hypothetical, not measured.

lessons.title: An API-complete workflow and qualification map
lessons.outcome: Navigate every pinned public TMB API without overstating untested features.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which prints an evidence map and the checks still required. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `tests/acceptance.R` and `tests/public_api.R` are the executable checks, and the course qualification ledger records where they actually ran.
lessons.verification: The evidence map marks the compiled, native, rpy2 and Spark layers as separate run records, and the uncertainty and invalid-input checks remain required.

lessons.title: Typed vectors, matrices, arrays and sparse inputs
lessons.outcome: Design a C++ data contract that preserves dimensions, indices and scientific meaning.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which shows R's column-major array order and the conversion to zero-based indices. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes declare typed inputs such as `DATA_MATRIX(covariance)` and `DATA_SPARSE_MATRIX(precision)` in `models/density_forms.cpp`, and their `check.R` compiles and checks them.
lessons.verification: R stores the 2-by-3 array column-major (a[2, 2] is 4), the group design matrix selects u[group] exactly and C++ indices are the R indices minus one.

lessons.title: Stable distribution helpers and mixtures
lessons.outcome: Evaluate probability terms stably without changing their statistical meaning.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares stable and direct log-sum computations. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile `models/stable_mixture.cpp`, and `check.R` compares its values and gradients with an independent log-density oracle.
lessons.verification: The log-sum-exp mixture matches the direct value, stays finite at -1000 where the direct form underflows, and the stable log difference recovers log 0.5.

lessons.title: Multivariate normals and Gaussian Markov fields
lessons.outcome: Choose covariance or precision interfaces and verify equivalent tiny densities.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which compares covariance and precision forms of a bivariate normal density and inspects an intrinsic precision. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile `models/density_forms.cpp`, and `check.R` compares its `MVNORM`, `GMRF`, `SCALE` and `VECSCALE` densities with dense formulas.
lessons.verification: Covariance and precision forms of the bivariate normal density agree to 1e-12, and treating a precision as a covariance changes the value by more than 0.1.

lessons.title: Separable arrays and scalar or vector scales
lessons.outcome: Compose normalized densities while preserving axis order and scale Jacobians.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks the scaled-density identity and a Kronecker covariance. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile `models/separable_array.cpp`, and `check.R` compares its `SEPARABLE` value and every correlation and scale gradient direction with a dense oracle.
lessons.verification: The scaled density equals the correlation density plus the sum of log scales, and the Kronecker covariance has 0.3, 0.7 and 0.21 in its first row.

lessons.title: Reporting and simulation inside the C++ model
lessons.outcome: Keep diagnostics, differentiable outputs and simulated observations aligned with the model.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which tabulates residuals and simulates conditional and unconditional group outcomes. In the separately prepared `tmb-local` project, `models/normal_mean.cpp` contains `REPORT`, `ADREPORT` and a `SIMULATE` block, and `tests/public_api.R` calls `obj$simulate()`.
lessons.verification: The companion prints residuals and simulates three new group effects, so unconditional outcomes vary with the simulated effects while conditional outcomes keep fixed ones.

lessons.title: AD-safe branches, transforms and numerical domains
lessons.outcome: Distinguish data-controlled logic, parameter-controlled logic and invalid arithmetic.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a piecewise gradient against finite differences and evaluates a stable softplus. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile `models/conditional.cpp`, and `check.R` checks its conditional tape crossings.
lessons.verification: The piecewise gradient of max(x, 0)^2 matches central differences to 1e-7, and the stable softplus stays finite at 1000 where the naive form overflows.

lessons.title: Atomic functions and custom derivative contracts
lessons.outcome: Design and test a custom derivative boundary without silently truncating derivatives.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which checks a reverse-mode derivative rule for x^4 against finite differences. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile `models/atomic_quartic.cpp`, and `check.R` checks its atomic value, gradient and Hessian.
lessons.verification: The reverse-mode rule 4x^3 times the adjoint matches finite differences to 1e-7, and a wrong rule that is exact at x = 1 is caught at the other test points.

lessons.title: C++ model families and end-to-end acceptance
lessons.outcome: Plan a qualified custom template using the appropriate authoring families.
lessons.lab: Run the base-R companion, which prints an acceptance plan and a coverage table. The separately prepared `tmb-cpp-api` probes compile all five family models under CppAD in `check.R`, separately from the nine-model `tmb-local` project.
lessons.verification: The acceptance plan maps each check to the failure it catches, and the coverage table shows a new primitive with checked mathematics but no compiled run.
